text:
ash: FYI support ticket from AcmeCorp — p95 and p99 latency spikes started ~10m after the canary runtime v3.4.0 rollout to 20% traffic :grimacing:
neha: ack, ticket id?
ash: ticket 84217, attaching their sample request IDs and timestamps in the thread
liam: grabbing graphs now — looks like p95 jumped from 180ms -> ~1.2s on the tenant's model route, p99 to ~2.6s. No error rate increase.
jules: any config changes besides kernel selector update in this release?
neha: release notes show: kernel selector tweak, scheduler tweak (aggressive prefetch off by default), and batching heuristics updated.
ash: support-bot pasted customer's request IDs: rQZ-9c2, rQZ-9c3, rQZ-9f0. timestamps ~3265432165-3265432180
liam: I can reproduce locally on canary pool when I replay their load (low qps but many short sequences). p99 spikes on cold kv-cache miss path and when sequence length 1-5.
ash: interesting — could be the batching heuristic change making tiny requests wait in a batch longer or hitting slow-path for tiny sequences.
neha: check per-route kernel selection telemetry: run query: `select * from runtime.telemetry where route='acme-prod' and ts between 3265432000 and 3265433300` — I see a kernel fallback at 3265432150 for ~8% of requests
liam: kernel fallback = slower FP path, matches the timing. Which commit toggled that?
jules: commit 7a9d3b made the selector prefer new kernel for small seqs, but we added a safety fallback on mismatch. That fallback had a lock contention bug under short-seq microbursts.
ash: timeline: canary deploy at 3265432100, customer report 3265432160, kernel fallback starts 3265432150. looks correlated.
neha: mitigation options: 1) roll canary forward to 0% (rollback), 2) hotfix to remove fallback lock, 3) route affected tenant away from canary via traffic-split override.
liam: I can patch a quick opt-out toggle to disable the safety fallback in runtime config and hot-reload on canary hosts — less blast radius than full rollback. Patch ready in branch `hotfix/fallback-optout`
jules: support escalation priority? customer is P2 (impacting latency but no errors). They requested either rollback or immediate workaround.
ash: I recommend immediate traffic-split override for Acme's route to point to stable pool, then we can apply opt-out on canary and validate. Support, can you request the traffic-split change?
support-bot: Filing internal request: route-ops ticket created #route-4567 to move `acme-prod` 100% -> stable pool. ETA 5m.
neha: while that's happening, liam — can you push opt-out to canary and share repro after? We want to avoid full rollback if possible.
liam: pushing toggle now to canary hosts (rolling restart small). Command: ``sudo systemctl restart runtime-canary && curl -XPOST http://canary-control/optout/fallback`` — will watch metrics.
(2m later) liam: pushed. initial samples show p95 back to ~170-200ms for replayed requests. p99 tail down to ~400ms and still dropping.
support-bot: route-ops confirms traffic-split done at 3265432540 — acme-prod now on stable. Customer reports improved latency in their next 10 requests.
jules: good. Next steps: 1) revert the lock in selector and add unit + stress tests around short-seq microbursts, 2) keep rollback/rollforward playbook updated, 3) add per-tenant canary override docs for support.
neha: add a telemetry alert rule to watch for kernel-fallback-rate > 1% for any route and sev2. Also add an automated rollback option if p99 > 1s for 5m post-rollout.
ash: I'll own the postmortem and release blocker. liam — please open PR with the fix and include perf test artifacts.
liam: on it. PR link: https://git.redwood/infra/runtime/pulls/892 — includes repro steps and flame graphs.
jules: closing the incident here. support: confirm customer closure and send a note about temporary mitigation. :thumbsup: 
support-bot: Customer updated and happy with outcome as of 3265432900. Closing ticket 84217.
neha: kudos team. Quick doc blurb for runbook: when canary-induced p95/p99 spike detected -> (a) traffic-split to stable, (b) opt-out toggle on canary, (c) rollback if unresolved in 15m.
ash: adding to runbook now and scheduling follow-up sync tomorrow to review tests and release gating. Thanks all.
